blocks.text: The Violation Tickets Dashboard in the Zscaler Security Operations (SecOps) platform offers visibility into your team's progress in identifying, managing, and resolving violation tickets. This dashboard enables you to view open violation tickets by severity, monitor ticket trends over time, track remediation efforts by the team, and ensure compliance goals are met.
To create this dashboard from a template, go to Explore > Dashboards > Template Gallery > Violation Tickets Dashboard. To learn more, see Using Dashboard Templates.
The charts and tables provide a detailed breakdown of violation tickets categorized by severity, time, and assignee.

blocks.item: Open Violation Tickets By Severity
The pie chart summarizes open violation tickets based on their severity level. Each color-coded sector represents a specific severity level, allowing you to quickly assess the risk.
The legend provides details for each category, including the category name, the count of open violation tickets, and the relative percentage of the total ticket volume.
The risk levels displayed on the pie chart are:
Critical (maroon): The total open violation tickets with the highest risk level.
High (red): The total open violation tickets with significant risk.
Medium (orange): The total open violation tickets with moderate risk.
Low (yellow): The total open violation tickets with low risk.
See image.
Open Violation Tickets Over Time
The time-series line chart provides a historical overview of open violation tickets, helping you identify trends in ticket resolution or accumulation over a specific period.

A downward slope confirms that the team is meeting compliance goals, while an upward or static trend serves as a prompt to adjust resources or investigate technical blockers in the remediation pipeline.
See image.
Click a date on the timeline, and click View Items to see a detailed list of all open violation tickets for the specific date.
See image.
Open Violation Tickets Progress Over Time
The multi-series line chart tracks the history of open violation tickets by severity level. The chart tracks three distinct severity levels, each represented by a color-coded line.
This visualization allows you to analyze the velocity and priority of a team's remediation efforts, and monitor the security posture over a timeline to facilitate data-driven decision-making.
Horizontal lines indicate no new tickets were opened, and no existing tickets were closed. A downward slope suggests that remediation processes are effective across all severity levels.
The risk levels displayed on the multi-series line chart are:
Critical (maroon): Open violation tickets with the highest risk level.
High (red): Open violation tickets with significant risk.
Medium (orange): Open violation tickets with moderate risk.
Low (yellow): Open violation tickets with low risk.
See image.
Click a date on the timeline, and click View Items to see a detailed list of all open violation tickets for the specific date and severity level.
See image.
Remediation Percentage by Assignee

The table provides a month-over-month performance comparison of how teams and individuals resolve violation tickets. The table lists the individuals or teams currently responsible for the violation tickets, the number of open versus closed violation tickets assigned to them, and the rate of ticket closure. This allows you to track the progress of ticket resolution, identify bottlenecks in the remediation workflow, and ensure accountability across teams.
